references.text: Jesus' sending of the twelve in Matthew contains similar instructions not to take gold, silver, copper, a bag, two tunics, sandals, or a staff – parallel to Luke's account of the mission's simplicity.

Mark's parallel account of the sending of the twelve, where Jesus commands them not to take anything on the way except a staff – no bread, no bag, no money in their belt, but they were allowed sandals and not two tunics.
At the sending of the seventy(-two), Jesus gives similar instructions: they are not to carry a money pouch, a bag, or sandals – reinforcing the principle of relying on God's provision.

Jesus refers back to this sending and asks the disciples if they lacked anything when he sent them out without a money pouch, a bag, or sandals. They answered no, confirming God's care during their mission.

Jesus' teaching in the Sermon on the Mount about not worrying about food, drink, or clothing, but seeking God's kingdom first – the theological foundation for the instruction to travel without supplies.
Paul expresses confidence that God will supply all their needs according to his riches in glory in Christ Jesus – the same principle of divine provision underlying Jesus' sending instructions.
